ja: だいにじゅうきゅうかい

p.src: Shi En stepped forward and said, “Please sit down, elder brother, and let me tell you the whole story of my troubles.” Wu Song said, “Young Warden, spare me the fine phrases. Just tell me plainly what matters.” Shi En said, “From childhood I learned some skill with spear and staff from masters of the martial world, and here in Mengzhou they gave me the sobriquet ‘Golden-Eyed Tiger Cub.’ Outside the eastern gate here lies a marketplace called the Forest of Delight. Merchants from Shandong and Hebei all come there to trade. There are around a hundred large inns and some twenty or thirty gambling houses and money exchanges. Formerly, relying first on my own skill and second on some eighty or ninety desperate convicts under my command in the prison camp, I opened a wine-and-meat shop there and supplied all the inns, gambling houses, and exchanges. Whenever a travelling courtesan came there, she first had to pay her respects to me before she was allowed to ply her trade. Every one of those establishments paid incidental dues each day. By the end of the month I could collect two or three hundred taels of silver—that was how I made my money. Recently, however, Instructor Zhang of this garrison returned from a posting in the eastern prefectures and brought a man here with him. The fellow’s surname is Jiang and his given name Zhong. He stands some nine feet tall, and so in the martial world they call him ‘Jiang the Gate God.’ Not only is he huge, but he is highly skilled: adept with spear and staff, quick with fist and foot, and best of all at wrestling. He boasts, ‘For three years I competed in wrestling on Mount Tai and never met my match. There is no one else like me beneath heaven!’ And so he came to seize my livelihood. I refused to yield, so the brute thrashed me with fists and feet, leaving me unable to rise from bed for two months. When you arrived the other day, elder brother, my head was still bandaged and my arm still in a sling; even now the scars have not faded. I had meant to gather men and fight him, but he has Instructor Zhang’s company of regular soldiers behind him. If trouble broke out, our prison camp would be in the wrong from the outset. Thus I have borne this boundless hatred without being able to avenge it. I have long heard that you are a true man, elder brother. If only you could vent this immeasurable grievance for me, I could close my eyes content even in death! I feared only that you were exhausted from your long journey and had not yet recovered your breath and strength. That is why I wished you to rest and recover for three or six months, and meant to discuss the matter only when your health and strength were fully restored. But my rustic servant unexpectedly let it slip and spoke out of turn, so I have told you the truth.”

p.src: When Wu Song had heard him out, he laughed heartily and asked, “How many heads and how many arms does this ‘Jiang the Gate God’ have?” Shi En replied, “He has only one head and two arms. How could he have more?” Wu Song laughed. “I thought he had three heads and six arms and possessed Nezha’s powers—that might have frightened me. But it turns out he has only one head and two arms! Since he does not have Nezha’s form, why should I fear him?” Shi En said, “It is only that I am weak and poorly trained, and could not overcome him.” Wu Song said, “I am not boasting. With the skill I possess, all my life I have fought only the toughest bullies under heaven, men who know neither morality nor justice. Now that you have told me this, what are we still doing here? If there is wine, bring it along for us to drink on the road. I shall go with you this very moment, and you can watch me finish that brute as I did the tiger. If my fists prove too heavy and kill him, I shall pay for his life with my own.” Shi En said, “Please sit a little longer, elder brother. Once my father has come out to meet you, we shall leave at once if we are to go; I dare not act rashly. Tomorrow we should first send someone there to make inquiries. If the man himself is at home, we can go the day after. If the brute is away, we can make other arrangements. If we go there for nothing and ‘beat the grass only to startle the snake,’ he will have time to lay his plans against us, and that would be bad.” Wu Song said impatiently, “Young Warden, no wonder he beat you! That is no way for a true man to conduct himself! If we are going, then let us go—why wait for today or tomorrow? If we mean to go, let us set out. Why fear his preparations?”

p.src: While Shi En was still trying in vain to restrain him, the elder warden emerged from behind a screen and called, “Good sir, I have been listening to you for some time. Today I have the good fortune to meet you, and for my foolish son it is as though the clouds had parted and the sun appeared. Please come to the rear hall and talk with me awhile.” Wu Song followed him inside. The elder warden said, “Please be seated, good sir.” Wu Song replied, “I am a convict. How could I dare sit as an equal with Your Honour?” The elder warden said, “You must not speak so, good sir. It is my foolish son’s great good fortune to have met you. Why stand on ceremony?” Hearing this, Wu Song made a bow apologizing for his discourtesy and sat down facing him. Shi En, however, remained standing before them. Wu Song asked, “Young Warden, why are you still standing?” Shi En replied, “My father is seated above to keep you company. Please make yourself at ease, elder brother.” Wu Song said, “If that is how it is, I cannot feel at ease.” The elder warden said, “Since you feel so, good sir, and there are no outsiders here...” He then told Shi En to sit as well. Servants brought out wine, delicacies, fruit, and dishes of food. The elder warden personally offered Wu Song a cup and said, “Who could fail to admire a hero such as you? My foolish son formerly conducted some business in the Forest of Delight, not from greed for money or profit, but truly to lend splendour to Mengzhou and add to its air of gallantry. Unexpectedly, ‘Jiang the Gate God’ has now relied on powerful backing and brute force to seize the place openly. None but a hero such as you can avenge this wrong and wipe away our hatred. If you will not disdain my foolish son, please drain this cup and accept four bows from him as he acknowledges you as his elder brother, thereby expressing his reverence.” Wu Song replied, “What talent or learning do I possess that I should dare accept such honours from the young warden? You would only be wasting all the fodder you have spent on Wu Song!” They then drank the wine, and Shi En bowed his head to the ground four times. Wu Song hurriedly returned the courtesy, and the two became sworn brothers. That day Wu Song drank merrily until he was thoroughly drunk. They had attendants help him to his room to rest, and nothing further need be said of it.

p.src: The next day, Shi En and his father conferred: “Wu Song was dead drunk last night and is surely suffering from the wine. How could we ask him to go today? Let us pretend that the man we sent to inquire found him away from home. We can put matters off for a day and attend to them afterward.” That day Shi En went to see Wu Song and said, “We had better not go today. I have sent someone to investigate and learned that the scoundrel is away from home. Tomorrow after the meal, I shall ask you to go, elder brother.” Wu Song said, “Going tomorrow is no great matter, but now I must endure another whole day of vexation.” After breakfast and tea, Shi En and Wu Song went for a leisurely stroll before the prison camp. When they returned to the guest room, they talked of spear techniques and tested one another’s skill with fists and staves. As noon drew near, Shi En invited Wu Song to his home and entertained him with only a few cups of wine, though the dishes served with the meal and wine were beyond counting. Wu Song wanted to drink, but when he saw that Shi En merely kept adding dishes and urging him to eat, he paid it little heed. After eating the midday meal, he rose, took his leave, and returned to sit in the guest room. Presently the same two servants came again to attend Wu Song at his bath. Wu Song asked, “Why did your young commandant offer me nothing but meat today, instead of bringing out more wine for me to drink? What was the reason?” A servant replied, “We dare not conceal it from you, Chief. This morning the senior and young commandants discussed asking you to go today, but they feared that you had drunk too much last night and might still be suffering from the wine, which could interfere with the important business. For that reason, they dared not bring out any wine. Tomorrow they mean to ask you to undertake the important business.” Wu Song said, “So they thought I was drunk and would spoil their great affair?” The servant said, “That is precisely what they reckoned.”

p.src: That night Wu Song could scarcely wait for dawn. He rose early, washed and groomed himself, wrapped a swastika-patterned kerchief around his head, donned an earth-colored cloth shirt, tied a red silk sash about his waist, bound his legs and knees, and put on hemp sandals with eight straps. He asked for a small plaster and placed it over the “golden brand” on his face. Shi En came early to invite him home for breakfast. When Wu Song had finished his tea and rice, Shi En said, “There are horses in the rear stable. We shall saddle one for you to ride.” Wu Song said, “My feet are not so dainty. What would I ride a horse for? There is only one thing I want you to do as I say.” Shi En said, “Just tell me, elder brother. How would I dare refuse?” Wu Song said, “Once you and I are out of the city, you must grant me my rule: ‘No three bowls, no passing the sign.’” Shi En said, “Elder brother, what does ‘No three bowls, no passing the sign’ mean? I do not understand.” Wu Song laughed. “I shall explain. Since you want me to thrash Jiang the Door God, once we leave the city, whenever we encounter a wineshop, you must treat me to three bowls of wine. If I have not had three bowls, I shall not pass its signboard. That is what I call ‘No three bowls, no passing the sign.’” Hearing this, Shi En thought, “The Forest of Delight lies fourteen or fifteen li from the east gate. By my reckoning, there are twelve or thirteen places selling wine along the way. If he drinks three bowls at every house, he will have swallowed fully thirty-five or thirty-six bowls by the time we arrive. What if elder brother gets drunk? How could that possibly do?” Wu Song laughed loudly. “You fear that once I am drunk, I shall have no skill; but it is when I have no wine that I have no skill. With one part wine in me, I have one part skill; with five parts wine, five parts skill. If I drink my full ten parts, there is no telling where all that strength comes from. Had drink not made me bold, how could I have killed that great tiger on Jingyang Ridge? I was thoroughly drunk then. That made it easy to strike: I had both strength and momentum.” Shi En said, “I never knew that was how you were, elder brother. We have plenty of fine wine at home. It was only because we feared that you might get drunk and spoil the affair that we dared not bring it out last night and invite you to drink deeply. Since you grow more capable after drinking, I shall have two servants take our fine wine, fruit, and dishes ahead and wait for us on the road. Then you and I can drink leisurely as we go.” Wu Song said, “Now that is exactly to my liking! If I am to thrash Jiang the Door God, let me fortify my courage a little. Without wine, how could I bring my techniques into play? This very morning I shall knock that scoundrel down for you and give everyone a hearty laugh!” Shi En immediately made preparations. He told two servants to shoulder hampers of food and loads of wine, gave them some copper coins, and sent them ahead. The senior commandant also secretly selected ten or twenty strong, sturdy men, instructed them all, and had them follow slowly behind as reinforcements.

p.src: Now Shi En and Wu Song left Anping Stockade and passed through the east gate of Mengzhou. After walking three or five hundred paces, they saw a wineshop beside the highway, its signboard already hanging beneath the eaves. The two servants carrying the food and wine were already waiting there. Shi En invited Wu Song inside to sit. The servants had already laid out the dishes and now strained and served the wine. Wu Song said, “I will not drink from little cups. Serve it in great bowls, and pour only three.” The servants set out large bowls and promptly filled them with wine. Without standing on ceremony, Wu Song drank three bowls in succession and rose. The servants hurriedly gathered up the vessels and rushed on ahead. Wu Song laughed. “That merely woke my belly a little. Let us be on our way.” The two left that wineshop and came out onto the road. It was then the seventh month. The summer heat had not yet faded, though the first autumn wind had begun to rise. They loosened their robes and went on. Before they had traveled much more than a li, they reached a place that was neither village nor town, where they soon saw another wine flag raised high among the trees. When they entered the grove to look, they found a little wineshop selling rustic brew. This is what they saw:

p.src: Beside an ancient road in a country hamlet, a wineshop stood by a stream. Dark willow shade lay beyond the door; graceful lotus blossoms filled the pond. The wine flag fluttered in the autumn breeze, while a short reed blind screened the searing sun. On a rack, porcelain jars brimmed pale and cool with rustic wine; before the stove, earthen crocks held newly steamed festival brew, fragrant and warm. Though opening a jar might not perfume ten li around, it ought at least to leave three neighboring households drunk.

p.src: At that moment, Shi En and Wu Song came to the door of a village wineshop. Shi En stopped and asked, “This is a little country tavern. Would you like a drink, brother?” Wu Song said, “Sour, salty, bitter, or astringent—it matters not. If it is wine, I must drink three bowls. If they will not serve me three, I shall simply pass their curtain by.” The two sat down, and the servant laid out fruit and dishes to accompany the wine. Wu Song drank three bowls in succession, then rose and left. The servant hurriedly gathered up the utensils and belongings and hastened after them. After leaving the tavern, they had gone scarcely another mile or two when they saw a second wineshop beside the road. Wu Song went in, drank another three bowls, and left. There is no need to belabor the tale. Wu Song and Shi En walked on together, and whenever they encountered a wineshop, Wu Song went in and drank three bowls. By the time they had visited some ten fine taverns, Shi En looked at Wu Song and saw that he was not very drunk. Wu Song asked Shi En, “How much farther is it to the Forest of Delight?” Shi En replied, “Not far now. You can see the grove ahead in the distance—that is the place.” Wu Song said, “Since we have arrived, wait for me elsewhere. I shall go and find him myself.” Shi En said, “That would be best. I have a place where I can stay. But take care, brother, and by no means underestimate your enemy.” Wu Song said, “There is no cause for concern. Just have the servant escort me. If there are any more wineshops ahead, I still mean to drink.” Shi En ordered the servant to continue escorting Wu Song. Shi En then went off alone.

p.src: Wu Song went another three or four miles at most and drank more than ten additional bowls of wine. It was now around noon. The day was hot, though a faint breeze was blowing. The wine began to rise in Wu Song, and he pulled open his cloth shirt. Though only half or two-thirds drunk, he pretended to be completely intoxicated, reeling forward and backward and lurching from side to side. When they reached the grove, the servant pointed and said, “At the T-junction just ahead is the tavern of Jiang the Gate God.” Wu Song said, “Since we are here, go and hide well out of the way. After I have knocked him down, you may all come.”

p.src: After another thirty or fifty paces, he soon saw a large tavern at the T-junction. A signpole stood beneath the eaves, from which hung a wine banner bearing four great characters: “Heyang Pleasures.” Turning to look, he saw a row of green-painted railings before the door and two gold-embroidered banners planted there. Five characters in gold were written on each, together reading: “Drunk, the world is vast; within the jar, the days and months are long.” On one side stood the meat counter, chopping blocks, knives, and other implements; on the other were the kitchen stoves where buns were steamed and firewood burned. Farther inside, three great wine vats stood in a row, half buried in the ground, each more than half full of wine; In the center stood the counter, and behind it sat a young woman. Her small bright headdress was inlaid with fish-bone ornament, half veiled by cloud-dark hair; Her narrow, finely tailored sleeves were dyed pomegranate red, lightly enclosing skin white as auspicious snow. p.src: Looking around the tavern, Wu Song saw five or seven serving men at work. Wu Song rapped on the table and called, “Where is the master who sells the wine?” The head waiter came over, looked at Wu Song, and asked, “How much wine would you like, sir?” Wu Song said, “Draw me two jiao of wine. Bring me a little first so I can taste it.” The waiter went to the counter and asked the woman to ladle out two jiao of wine. She poured it into a vessel, and he swirled a bowlful and brought it over, saying, “Taste the wine, sir.” Wu Song picked it up and sniffed it, then shook his head. “No good, no good! Bring me another!”

p.src: Swallowing his anger, the waiter took the wine back to the counter and said, “Mistress, just change it once more for something better. Do not stoop to quarrel with him. This customer is drunk and seems bent only on causing trouble. Just give him some of the very best.” The woman ladled out yet another grade of excellent wine and gave it to the waiter. He set the vessel before Wu Song and again poured him a bowl. Wu Song drank it and said, “Now this wine has a little character.” Then he asked, “Waiter, what is your master’s surname?” The waiter replied, “Jiang.” Wu Song said, “Then why is his surname not Li?” Hearing this, the woman said, “Where did this lout get drunk before coming here to provoke us?” The waiter said, “He is plainly some uncouth out-of-towner who knows nothing. Pay no heed to his farting nonsense!” Wu Song asked, “What did you say?” The waiter replied, “We were speaking among ourselves. Never mind us, sir; just drink your wine.”

p.src: Wu Song said, “Waiter, tell that woman behind the counter to come down and keep me company while I drink.” The waiter shouted, “Do not talk such nonsense! She is the master’s wife.” Wu Song said, “So what if she is the master’s wife? There is no harm in her keeping me company while I drink!” The woman flew into a rage and cursed, “You damned brute! You thieving wretch fit only to die!” She pushed open the counter gate and was about to rush out.

p.src: Wu Song had already stripped off his coarse, earth-colored shirt and tucked its upper half into his breast. Then, with a single splash, he poured the bucket of wine onto the ground, sprang behind the counter, and caught the woman just as she came at him. Wu Song's grip was like iron; how could she possibly struggle free? Wu Song caught her round the waist with one hand, crushed her headdress to powder with the other, seized her cloudlike coiffure, hauled her bodily over the counter, and flung her straight into a vat of cloudy wine. There came a tremendous splash; the poor woman had been pitched headlong into the great wine vat. With a bound, Wu Song vaulted out from behind the counter. Several brawny tavern hands, quicker on their feet than the rest, rushed at Wu Song. As soon as one came within reach, Wu Song lightly snatched him up, dragged him close, seized him with both hands, and tossed him into another great wine vat, wedging him inside. Another tavern hand charged him; Wu Song caught him by the head, swung him aside, and threw him into a wine vat as well. Two more tavern hands came at him, but Wu Song felled them with one punch and one kick. The first three men, each stuck in a wine vat, could not struggle out. The other two lay on the ground, unable even to crawl. These ruffian attendants had been beaten into a panic; one of the cleverer ones managed to flee. Wu Song said, “That scoundrel is surely going to fetch Jiang the Gate God. I shall go meet him and knock him down on the highway, so everyone can have a laugh.” Wu Song strode out after him.

p.src: The ruffian ran straight off and reported the matter to Jiang the Gate God. When Jiang the Gate God heard the news, he started in alarm, kicked over his folding chair, threw aside his fly whisk, and came boring his way out. Wu Song was coming to meet him, and the two encountered each other on the broad highway. Jiang the Gate God was tall and powerful, but lately wine and women had sapped his strength. Already shaken by the news, he came rushing up without checking his stride. How could he match a tiger-strong man like Wu Song, who had moreover deliberately set himself to deal with him? When Jiang the Gate God saw Wu Song, he assumed the man was drunk and charged heedlessly at him. Before one could tell it, it was done: Wu Song feinted at Jiang the Gate God's face with both fists, then suddenly turned and ran. Jiang the Gate God flew into a rage and lunged after him. Wu Song whipped up a flying kick that struck Jiang the Gate God in the lower belly; he clutched himself with both hands and sank into a crouch. Wu Song wheeled round; his right foot was already in the air and flew straight into Jiang the Gate God's temple. The kick landed squarely, and Jiang toppled backward. Wu Song followed with a step, planted his foot on the man's chest, raised a fist as large as a vinegar jar, and began pounding Jiang the Gate God's face. This was the fighting trick already mentioned for overcoming Jiang the Gate God: first feint with the fists, then turn away; next launch the left foot, and once it strikes, spin round and send up the right. This maneuver was known as “Jade-Ring Step and Mandarin-Duck Kicks.” This was Wu Song's own hard-won mastery, and no trifling skill. He beat Jiang the Gate God until the man begged for mercy on the ground. Wu Song shouted, “If you want me to spare your life, you need only agree to three demands.” From the ground Jiang the Gate God cried, “Have mercy on me, good sir! Never mind three—even if there were three hundred, I would agree to them all!” Wu Song pointed at Jiang the Gate God and stated his three demands. And so it came about that, under a changed appearance, one would go seeking a master, while another, with hair shorn level with the brows, would go forth to kill. But what three demands did Wu Song make? Listen to the next chapter and all will be revealed.
